The first: cap the number of points that any user can get for a comment. Reddit is mostly the crap-fest that it is because idiots vie for imaginary internet points, and puns/one-liners/tired memes get the most upvotes. The exact same thing will eventually happen here, especially as a large number of redditors are jumping ship.

So, do something simple: cap the max points for any comment at, say, 50. Once it reaches this point it can go no higher. The people invested in internet points will shit a brick, but it'll encourage them to stay away from Voat and instead remain on reddit where, I believe, they belong. Reddit becomes the place to internet-dick-measure, Voat becomes the place where discussion is more important than points (since you can only get so many points anyway). This will also mean that even should jokes rise to the top, they can't completely drown out the actual, semi-serious dialogue that follows.

Second idea: every downvote costs YOU a point. That's right, if you want to downvote you not only have to rack up a certain number of points, like in the current system, but you'll have to spend one of your own precious points in the process. It'll make people think twice before downvoting and more importantly, it'll put an end to the downvote brigades that plague reddit. The brigades are only made possible because hundreds or thousands of accounts can downvote willy-nilly without any repercussions whatsoever.

For those who're concerned that trolls/SJWs/whatever won't be downvoted, by default they will because their commentary will always remain at 0. If you really want to see them hit negative numbers, you've got to be invested enough in the act to pay the price. If you aren't that invested then you don't have any business trying to shut them down, now do you?

I think the biggest problem with reddit is that the voting system is deliberately designed to cater to the lowest common denominator, to group-think, and to in jokes. I think these two ideas would go a long way to making that a non-issue on Voat.
You should probably post this to /v/ideasforvoat, not /v/askvoat.

The problem with the first idea you posted is that comment points are used to measure how high up the comment will be ranked. What should happen instead is that after your comment reaches 50 points, the points stop going to your account but the comment still gets more points.

Netflix and the future of television

Although lengthy, this is such a great article about how television has evolved up to this point, and how it will continue evolving.

I remember when I was ten-years old, back in the mid-90s, when computers were nothing more than kilobytes, and internet was nothing more than pay-by-the-hour and "you've got mail," my art teacher (who was really good friends with my science teacher) presented us with an assignment. He said, "I want you to think of an invention, and then I want you to draw what this invention would look like, and present the drawing to the class, explaining what it was and how it works. The invention that I came up with -- because I was such a cinephile, even at a young age -- was a television that functioned similar to a desktop computer. A television with a keyboard, essentially. And when I explained it to the class, I sold it as something that was virtually impossible. I said, "Which movie do you want to see? Any movie. Pick one. Type it in, and it will play on your television. Even if the movie is still at the movie theater. No, wait! Even if the movie hasn't even been released in theaters yet! You can still type it in and watch it!" My art teacher thought I was insane. "You can just watch anything? Just type it in and you can watch it? Even if the movie hasn't been released yet? How in the world would anyone be able to do that?"

I wish I had kept that shitty drawing I did in fifth grade. If I still had it, I would try to track him down. "Insane, you say? Ahem. Netflix, Hulu (Plus), iTunes, Amazon Prime, Swarm, YouTube, Vimeo, DailyMotion, The Pirate Bay, Kickass, SolarMovie, etc. -- oh, and about seeing movies before they are released, I have two words and a number for you: The Expendables 3."
